overview: Ingersoll Rand designs, manufactures, markets and services mission-critical air, gas, fluid, and specialty pumping and compression equipment, along with related aftermarket parts, consumables and services, under a multi-brand portfolio (Ingersoll Rand, Gardner Denver, Nash, ARO, Haskel, ILC Dover, Milton Roy and dozens of others). The company, headquartered in Davidson, North Carolina and formerly Gardner Denver Holdings before renaming in 2020 following its 2020 merger with the Ingersoll-Rand industrial segment, operates two segments: Industrial Technologies & Services (roughly 79% of revenue; air/gas compressors, vacuum and blower products, fluid transfer, power tools) and Precision & Science Technologies (roughly 21%; precision pumps, life-sciences fluid handling, and hydrogen/clean-energy components). It sells globally through direct sales and independent distributors to industrial, medical, water/wastewater, chemical processing, food & beverage, and clean-energy end markets.

business_model.summary: Ingersoll Rand generates revenue from original equipment sales (compressors, pumps, blowers, vacuum systems) plus a large and growing aftermarket business of parts, consumables and services that runs on the installed base independent of new-equipment cycles (aftermarket is roughly 35-40% of total revenue). Growth is driven organically through pricing, volume and a decentralized 'IRX' (Ingersoll Rand Execution Excellence) operating playbook, and inorganically through a high-velocity pipeline of bolt-on acquisitions (typically founder-owned niche players bought at ~9-10x pre-synergy EBITDA and re-rated toward mid-teens ROIC within about three years) plus occasional larger transformational deals (e.g., the $2.325B ILC Dover acquisition in 2024 that expanded the addressable market into life sciences).

revenue_streams.name: Aftermarket parts, consumables & services (cuts across both segments)
New equipment / OEM (cuts across both segments)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - industrial manufacturers, medical/life-sciences device and biopharma customers, water/wastewater utilities, chemical processors, food & beverage producers, and clean-energy/hydrogen developers, sold via direct sales force and independent distributors
business_model.geographic_mix: Global manufacturing and sales footprint with meaningful exposure to the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific (including China); management has flagged China as the most difficult pricing environment currently, with overcapacity pressuring local pricing

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest global players in air/gas compression, vacuum and blower equipment, and a growing niche leader in precision pumping and life-sciences fluid handling following the ILC Dover acquisition; the broader compression/vacuum/blower marketplace remains highly fragmented across product technologies and channels rather than dominated by a single player

moat_factors.description: A large, aging installed base of compressors and pumps generates recurring, higher-margin parts and service revenue (roughly 35-40% of sales) that is stickier and less cyclical than new-equipment sales

moat_factors.factor: M&A platform and IRX operating system
moat_factors.description: A repeatable, disciplined process for sourcing proprietary (often founder-owned) bolt-on targets at attractive multiples and improving them through a standardized lean operating playbook (100-day sprints, weekly IMPACT Daily Management) is a differentiated, difficult-to-replicate capability compounding scale over time
Nine P&L leaders reporting to the CEO with ~60 sub-P&Ls underneath enables fast integration of acquisitions and close-to-customer decision-making versus more centralized industrial conglomerates

Multi-brand strategy (Gardner Denver, Nash, ARO, Haskel, Milton Roy, ILC Dover, etc.) allows serving many fragmented niches without diluting individual brand equity, but no single brand carries category-defining pricing power comparable to a premium industrial leader
Products in life sciences and medical end markets require customer qualification cycles that create switching costs once designed into a validated process

weaknesses: Highly fragmented end markets with several large, well-capitalized competitors (Atlas Copco, Dover, IDEX) limit pricing power and market share gains through organic means alone

Recent organic growth has been weak to negative (organic revenue averaged roughly a 1.4% YoY decline over the past two years) with 2026 guidance calling for only 1-3% organic growth, raising questions about underlying demand independent of M&A
Heavy reliance on continued acquisition volume to sustain growth narrative; any slowdown in deal flow or deterioration in acquired-company integration would expose softer organic trends
China pricing pressure from regional overcapacity has weighed on Industrial Technologies & Services margins (down 180bps YoY in Q2 2026)
No dominant, singular technological moat comparable to aerospace-grade certification businesses; competitive advantage rests more on execution and capital allocation than on hard-to-replicate IP

growth_drivers: Continued high-velocity bolt-on M&A pipeline - management has cited roughly 11 additional transactions under LOI as of mid-2026, alongside recently announced/closed deals (Lone Star Blowers, Fai Filtri) that add scale and aftermarket capability

Aftermarket/services mix shift - growing installed base (particularly boosted by ILC Dover and other recent life-sciences and precision-pump acquisitions) supports higher-margin, more resilient recurring revenue over time

Precision & Science Technologies momentum - life sciences orders grew low-double-digits organically in Q2 2026 and Precision Technologies grew mid-single-digits, outpacing the legacy Industrial Technologies & Services segment

Clean-energy/hydrogen and water/wastewater secular demand - IR's precision pumping, hydrogen compression and dosing technologies are positioned for growth in clean-energy infrastructure and municipal water investment

Tariff/price pass-through and reshoring - company has stood up a dedicated 'tariff war room' to manage ~$150M of tariff costs via pricing/surcharges and is realigning sourcing toward in-region supply chains, which could benefit from broader reshoring/industrial capex trends
Margin expansion in Precision & Science Technologies (up 200bps YoY in Q2 2026) from operational excellence execution, a template management aims to replicate more broadly

business.description: Underlying organic revenue has been roughly flat to slightly negative over the trailing two years; FY2026 guidance embeds only 1-3% organic growth with the bulk of headline growth coming from M&A, FX and tariff pass-through pricing

Dozens of bolt-on deals plus larger transactions (ILC Dover for $2.325B) create ongoing integration execution risk; any misstep in absorbing acquired businesses into IRX could impair expected synergies and ROIC targets
Regional overcapacity has pushed China pricing negative, and management characterizes normalization as a multi-period process, not a quick fix
Numerous credible competitors (Atlas Copco, Dover, IDEX, Flowserve, Xylem) compete on product quality, efficiency, service and local presence, limiting structural pricing power

financial.description: Serial acquisition strategy is funded partly with debt; net debt/EBITDA around 1.9x and debt/equity around 0.48x as of the latest screen are moderate but could rise with continued large-scale dealmaking

Interest coverage of ~5.8x is solid but a heavier acquisition pace funded with incremental debt in a higher-for-longer rate environment would pressure coverage and free cash flow available for buybacks/dividends
Meaningful non-US revenue and manufacturing base creates FX translation risk; 2026 guidance embeds roughly a 1% currency tailwind that could reverse

regulatory.description: Company estimates roughly $150M of gross tariff cost impact in 2026 it is working to fully offset via pricing/surcharges; incremental tariff escalation or an inability to pass through costs would compress margins
Manufacturing operations globally are subject to environmental and industrial safety regulation across multiple jurisdictions, with attendant compliance costs

ILC Dover and other precision/life-science products are subject to customer and regulatory (e.g., FDA-adjacent) qualification standards; failure to maintain qualifications could impair sales in that segment

macro.description: New-equipment orders are sensitive to global industrial production, capital spending cycles and manufacturing PMI; a broader industrial slowdown would pressure the larger Industrial Technologies & Services segment
Slower China industrial activity and local overcapacity have already produced negative pricing; a deeper China slowdown would be a incremental drag

Trades at a premium multiple (trailing P/E ~29.7x, forward P/E ~19.7x per latest screen) versus underlying organic growth in the low single digits; a re-rating could occur if the market grows skeptical of M&A-driven growth sustainability or if rates rise, both compressing multiples and raising the cost of continued dealmaking
Broader US trade policy shifts (beyond the currently modeled $150M impact) could alter input costs, supply chains and end-customer capex decisions across IR's global footprint

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global industrial compression, vacuum, blower and precision fluid-handling markets are growing at low-to-mid single digit rates, supported by secular demand in life sciences/biopharma, clean energy (hydrogen), water/wastewater infrastructure and general industrial reshoring, but tempered by soft near-term global industrial production and China overcapacity/pricing pressure
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - Industrial Technologies & Services (new equipment) tracks industrial capex and manufacturing activity, while the aftermarket business and Precision & Science Technologies (life sciences, precision pumps) are comparatively more resilient and less tied to the capex cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - direct balance sheet impact is manageable given moderate leverage (~1.9x net debt/EBITDA, ~0.48x debt/equity), but a heavy reliance on continued M&A funding makes the cost and availability of debt capital relevant to the growth algorithm, and the premium equity multiple is vulnerable to rate-driven compression

recent_developments.event: Reported Q2 2026 results: revenue of $2.05 billion (+8.5% YoY, +4.1% organic) beat consensus by ~4.5%; adjusted EPS of $0.86 beat estimates by 3.6% (some sources cite $0.77-$0.86 range across reporting periods); total orders of $2.04 billion (+5.3% YoY, +1.6% organic); stock declined on the print despite the beat due to margin compression and organic growth concerns

Raised FY2026 revenue growth guidance to 4.5%-6.5% (implying ~1-3% organic growth, ~1% FX tailwind, ~2.5% from acquisitions); maintained adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.13-$2.19 billion and adjusted EPS guidance of $3.45-$3.57, with EPS expected to finish near the high end

Announced acquisitions of Lone Star Blowers (US blower manufacturer) and Fai Filtri, adding to aftermarket and core technology capabilities; management disclosed a robust M&A pipeline with roughly 11 additional transactions under Letter of Intent

Segment detail: Industrial Technologies & Services revenue of $1.62B (+9% reported, +4% organic) with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 26.8% (down 180bps YoY on China pricing pressure and growth investments); Precision & Science Technologies revenue of $426.7M (+8% reported, +4% organic) with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% (up 200bps YoY)

Management stood up a dedicated tariff mitigation 'war room,' targeting to neutralize an estimated ~$150 million of 2026 tariff cost impact through pricing/surcharges and supply-chain realignment toward in-region sourcing; additional IEEPA tariff refunds expected in H2 2026 are treated as upside not yet in guidance

Stock down roughly 7.9% YTD and ~27.8% below its 52-week high of $100.96 (set Feb 13, 2026), underperforming the S&P 500 materially amid investor concern over weak organic growth (organic revenue averaged a ~1.4% YoY decline over the trailing two years) and margin compression in the largest segment

Closed the transformational $2.325 billion acquisition of ILC Dover (life-sciences and space-industry fluid/containment solutions), expanding Ingersoll Rand's addressable market into an estimated $65 billion of new, fragmented niches; also closed several smaller bolt-ons (Complete Air and Power Solutions, Del PD Pumps & Gear, Fruvac) around the same time

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Vicente Reynal described China pricing softness as a 'timing issue' driven by regional overcapacity, with prices expected to move from negative low-single-digits toward flat over time (though not converging to North America/Europe levels), while reaffirming continued investment in 'China for China' localized applications. Management emphasized confidence in delivering full-year commitments on the back of building order momentum, expects tariff pricing/surcharges to offset costs roughly one-for-one with no net bottom-line impact, and continues to frame Precision & Science Technologies (particularly Life Sciences) as the faster-growing, higher-margin growth engine relative to the larger Industrial Technologies & Services segment.

bull_case: Proven, repeatable bolt-on M&A engine (IRX operating system) with a disciplined ~9-10x pre-synergy entry multiple and a deep pipeline (~11 deals under LOI) provides a visible runway for continued inorganic growth and margin improvement

Growing aftermarket/recurring revenue base (~35-40% of sales) and increasing mix shift toward higher-margin Precision & Science Technologies (life sciences, precision pumps) improve earnings quality and resilience versus a pure industrial-cyclical peer

Management has a strong long-term value-creation track record (enterprise value up >8x over CEO Vicente Reynal's tenure since the Gardner Denver era) and continues to execute tariff mitigation to protect margins
Transformational deals like ILC Dover expand the addressable market by tens of billions of dollars into structurally growing end markets (biopharma, life sciences, clean energy/hydrogen)
Moderate leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~1.9x, debt/equity ~0.48x, interest coverage ~5.8x) leaves balance sheet capacity to keep funding the acquisition strategy without excessive financial risk
bear_case: Organic growth has been weak to negative for two years running, and 2026 guidance embeds only 1-3% organic growth - raising the question of how much of the growth story is genuinely durable versus manufactured by acquisitions and price/FX

Industrial Technologies & Services margin compression (down 180bps YoY in Q2 2026) driven by China overcapacity and pricing pressure could persist longer than management's 'timing issue' framing suggests
Continued reliance on debt-funded serial acquisitions carries real integration risk, and any slowdown in deal flow, a bad deal, or credit-market tightening would directly hit the primary growth lever

Stock trades at a premium multiple (trailing P/E ~29.7x) despite underwhelming organic performance and sits ~28% below its 52-week high, suggesting the market is already discounting execution risk and could re-rate further if the M&A-driven growth algorithm disappoints

Tariff exposure (~$150M gross 2026 impact) depends on successful, sustained price/surcharge pass-through; failure to fully offset costs, or new escalation in trade policy, would pressure already-compressing margins
